raw_findings.summary: Product/docs/hygiene recon of Touch, every claim re-verified on disk (no facts inherited from the earlier aborted touch-repo-recon run). Two blockers: (1) CLAUDE.md — the file every fresh session auto-loads — states a false repo inventory, points only at the two orchestration skills, and never mentions inception.md, the 903-line normative touch-aggregator plan, the 229-line v0 touch-monitor-spawn plan, or the m-orchestrator/touch-orchestrate skills, so the next implementer re-derives a design already settled by ~1.1M tokens of research; (2) `.touch/` is not gitignored (verified via git check-ignore) in a repo with zero commits, and inception.md:115-119 says that store holds unredacted transcript content — any `git add -A` after the first code item bakes secrets into commit #1, which cannot be reverted away. Majors: no initial-commit definition and `git commit` currently fails outright (user.name/user.email unset locally and in /home/agent/.gitconfig; `git add -An` stages 45 paths; this run's events.jsonl/.watcher-state.json are mutating right now); README/CLAUDE.md promise "pause" that inception §4 proves cannot exist and "restart" is defined two incompatible ways (inception resumeFromRunId vs touch-orchestrate fresh attempt+1) while v0 implements neither; both CLAUDE.md:127-130 and inception.md:54-56 claim the task folders are foreign `omnigent` history when all three orch-config wf_dir paths are `-home-laniakea-Projects-touch` (this repo, this machine) — actively telling implementers to discount the only real data Touch must render; a user-directed normative model policy (Opus 5 @ xhigh for research/implementation roles, Fable reserved for synthesizer/main terminal/final review, divider pin an explicit open decision) exists solely inside the aborted touch-repo-recon workflow script and was dropped from this run's perspective list, so it will be lost unless the synthesizer carries it forward; and forensics on the event streams confirm touch-aggregator has only a `stage:complete state:running` line (no script anywhere emits the terminal `orchestrator complete done`) plus a fabricated `research plan failed "loop exited -> synthesis"` nine minutes before `synthesis plan done "plan written"` — the repo's flagship success is on record as a failure, while touch-repo-recon (3 of 6 findings, empty plan/ and report/, hand-typed stop event) is indistinguishable from a complete run. Verified-good: all four monitoring test suites pass, CLAUDE.md's port/wf_dir precedence lines match the code exactly, and CLI 2.1.220 matches inception's pin. Five decisions are handed to the synthesizer (restart semantics, role→model table, watcher-state tracking, one README or two, branch name + commit boundary) plus hard preconditions: gitignore edit before anything creates `.touch/`, git identity set, no commit while a watcher is writing.

Reviewed the whole monitoring module (status.sh, monitor_server.py, decision_watcher.py, monitor.html, monitoring.md, 4 test suites — all 4 pass) adversarially, verifying suspicions empirically in throwaway dirs under /tmp/claude-1000. 14 findings: 1 blocker, 4 major, 7 minor, 2 nits.

The blocker is a design decision Touch must make before writing any code: the server binds 0.0.0.0 with no authentication and no Origin check — I verified a cross-origin WebSocket upgrade (Origin: https://evil.example.com) is accepted and replays the full event history, and that /tasks//health answer any Host. That is tolerable for a read-only dev dashboard, but README.md requires pause/restart/terminate controls and touch-orchestrate SKILL.md §4 specifies the UI writing stop actions into .touch/control.jsonl. Bolting a write path onto this posture lets any page in the user's browser (WebSockets bypass SOP) terminate the user's agents.

Three majors are architectural gaps between the module and the touch-orchestrate skill that was drafted after both existing plans, so neither plan reflects them. (a) decision_watcher.py is hard-wired to a Workflow journal.jsonl, but touch-orchestrate mandates background Agent-tool spawns for TaskStop-ability — verified those produce no journal (~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/ contains only workflows/), so stoppability and deterministic monitoring are currently mutually exclusive. (b) The event schema is flat (plan → agent rows) with no parent/child edges and MARKER parses only [monitor], not [touch] name=/parent=/root=, so README's n8n-like graph is not derivable from events.jsonl at all; the frontend's "topology" is a heuristic over splitting a label string on " #". (c) An unknown ?task= silently falls back to the server's default state dir — verified streaming another task's events over /ws — which the frontend's FRONTEND-5 fix only papers over cosmetically, and which becomes a wrong-target hazard once task names route control actions.

The fourth major is a live defect: decision_watcher's emit() never creates STATE_DIR (the SHELL-6 mkdir -p fix went into status.sh only), so if the backgrounded watcher wins the launch-order race against the first seeding status.sh call it dies instantly on its heartbeat with an unhandled FileNotFoundError (reproduced), leaving the run with zero deterministic events and no detection.

Minors cover real but lower-stakes issues: unlocked concurrent appends to events.jsonl corrupt lines once a detail exceeds the 8KiB buffer (measured: 19/20 lines survived at 60KB detail) and corrupted lines are silently dropped by both the server and the browser with no counter anywhere; the dashboard calls render() per event and never trims the log, making replay quadratic; the watcher lacks the journal-truncation sentinel the server has (D10), so a shrunk journal stalls it forever; token accounting re-globs and fully re-parses every running agent's transcript at 1Hz; malformed config caps kill the watcher at import where the server handles the same class cleanly (SERVER-2); /file has no size cap. Test coverage has a structural weakness — several test_watcher.py "tests" re-implement the logic inline and assert on Python literals, so they cannot fail on regression, and emit(), main()'s tail loop, and the entire server request path are untested (which is precisely why findings 1 and 5 shipped).

The findings file closes with an explicit copy-verbatim vs. do-not-inherit split for the reconciled plan: keep the append-only stream with full replay, torn-tail handling, monotonic token deltas + message-id dedup across session rotations, realpath containment + CSP sandbox on served files, escape-first rendering, and source-keyed checkpointing; do not inherit the network posture, the unknown-task fallback, the 1Hz full re-parse, the render-everything frontend loop, unlocked appends, the flat schema as a graph model, or the journal-only event source.

Reviewed the four skills plus both workflow templates as the protocol Touch must render and drive, and validated them at runtime rather than only on paper: I replayed the real touch-aggregator event stream and ran the shipped decision_watcher.py against two synthetic Workflow journals in /tmp (a fully green serial implement run and a parallel sub-plan run). Three runtime defects fall out that the prior recon did not reach and that directly corrupt the entities Touch renders. (1) BLOCKER: any plan whose agents return no passed/approved verdict — every research fan-out and every Divide phase — closes its card "failed", and a completely green implement run is then declared "run failed" by the watcher; proven both in the real successful aggregator run ("research plan failed loop exited -> synthesis") and in simulation ("divide plan failed", "orchestrator complete failed"). (2) execute-research runs never produce a completion event at all (run_outcome can never go terminal when the last plan has no decisive verdict), so the completed aggregator run replays today as still running. (3) The parallel sub-plan mode that implement-plan explicitly supports makes plan cards flap to "failed" via the serial-only last_plan heuristic, and a card closed failed has no reopen path. Beyond those, the protocol has structural gaps for a UI/controller: no machine-readable topology anywhere (perspectives, sub-plan partition, phases, models and attempt budget exist only inside the JS or as prose markdown), which also makes m-orchestrator's "seed a card per sub-plan before launching" impossible as implement-plan itself admits; and sub-plan identity is re-derived by an LLM on every run with no re-entry argument, so the README's "restart loop" verb cannot be expressed at all. Attempt bookkeeping loses evidence in two ways: critique and the final scope audit only see the last attempt's files_changed (earlier-attempt edits ship unreviewed and then trip the final gate), and a dead/stopped implementer writes no findings file so the next attempt re-runs an identical prompt. Smaller but concrete: unvalidated divider ids are used as filesystem paths, shell arguments and monitoring plan ids (traversal / reserved-card hijack); final-gate decision text announces a critique that never spawns; the documented stage=-omission fallback provably never matches the templates' quoted status.sh line; MAX_ATTEMPTS and the watcher's caps are unsynced; the event stream carries no model/phase; the ownership guard is string equality. I also re-verified the prior run's hinge fact live — TaskList returned "No tasks found" while six Workflow researchers were running — so touch-orchestrate's ledger/TaskStop discipline remains unsatisfiable for the skill pair, and the whole prior findings file remains open since the skills are unchanged. 16 findings written to the task folder.

Reviewed the plan corpus (touch-aggregator T1-T23/D1-D14, touch-monitor-spawn P1-P12/G1-G9, inception.md sections 6-7) against the current repo, the newer touch-orchestrate skill, and the live substrate. 15 findings: 2 blockers, 8 major, 5 minor.

First, a negative result worth recording: every line anchor the two plans cite into .claude/shared/monitoring/ was re-checked and ALL resolve correctly (test_shell.py:155, status.sh:34-40, monitor.html:287, decision_watcher.py:138-152/:636-638/:682-688, monitor_server.py:199-212/:225-241/:279-310). Anchor rot is not a problem here.

The two blockers are about supersession and about the session-class model. (PLANS-1) implement-plan takes exactly ONE plan_file, yet both plans declare themselves consumable as-is, and they claim overlapping files under different module names (transcript.py vs ingest.py, util.py vs tailer.py, hookpack/ vs hooks/, server+routes vs server, plus ~10 shared files) - the file-ownership divider cannot resolve this. (PLANS-2) D1 says observed sessions get no control affordances "not even kill" and T14 makes foreign-session control 403 server-side; but the v0 plan defers the owned-session spawner, so every v0 session is observed, and v0's entire feature is a Stop button. The resolution exists only implicitly in the touch-orchestrate skill (the model polls .touch/control.jsonl itself) - that is a third "cooperating" class that must be added to D1 explicitly, with an evidence rule for promoting a session into it.

Empirically verified defects: git stash create prints "You do not have the initial commit yet", emits no sha, and exits 0 on this commitless repo, so T14's checkpoint silently records nothing (PLANS-9); real agent prompts begin with a newline before the marker ('\n[monitor] plan=research stage=sessiondata...'), so T8's anchored ^\[monitor\] regex and the skill's "FIRST line" rule both fail - the working watcher deliberately uses unanchored finditer (PLANS-10); the archived runs' wf_dirs, journals and 17-hex agent transcripts all still exist on disk, so T20's unconditional "archived - source transcripts unavailable" label and the CLAUDE.md omnigent claim are both wrong (PLANS-5); and the touch-aggregator events.jsonl carries six researchers all labelled "research #1" with 8-hex truncated ids, so Part F's "six distinctly labelled nodes" acceptance is unreachable through the legacy path and would be rejected outright by a D3 17-hex validator (PLANS-6).

Also major: G4 silently drops {runId,key,ordinal} from the ref union while claiming to be "exactly as D4" (PLANS-3); T11's path-parameter endpoints contradict D9.3's explicit "no path parameters" and T4's dict router (PLANS-4); the control file and spawn ledger have no discoverable address from a session the aggregator found via ~/.claude/sessions (PLANS-7); and P11's hook pack has no delivery path in v0 since the spawner is deferred and hook hot-reload is Part E's unsettled experiment #2 (PLANS-8).

Sequencing recommendation (PLANS-15): hand implement-plan ONE reconciled plan whose phase 1 is monitoring-only with no control verbs - scaffold, tailer, store, sessions, ingest, agents - which are the only six items fully ready as written, then gate the control plane on PLANS-2 + PLANS-7 + the Part E #2 experiment. Part F's single acceptance criterion spans three phases and should be restated per phase. Two prerequisites belong at the top of the plan and are in neither: make the initial git commit, and add an item that owns SKILL.md alongside a conformance test.

Audited all 161 prior findings (110 aggregator + 51 repo-recon), both plans, and the driver digest, then re-measured the corpus's load-bearing claims against the live substrate. Four findings are structural: (1) the 51 repo-recon findings — including five blockers about the spawn/stop contract, control-file paths, and the missing module-interface contract — have zero disposition in either plan, because both plans predate that run; (2) D8's normative rule "journal `result` is an opaque string, never parsed as JSON" (from SESSIONDATA-10) is falsified by every journal on disk — all seven results in wf_829e6f58-b2f are structured dicts — and contradicts `decision_watcher.py:370-447`, the verdict mapper the same plan tells implementers to copy; (3) Part E item 2 (hook hot-reload for running sessions) has still never been probed, yet the entire v0 control story hangs on it: v0 defers the owned-session spawner, the cooperative control.jsonl stop cannot be polled during a Workflow run (SKILLS-2), so if hooks only apply at spawn, v0 ships with no working stop at all; (4) the aggregator plan's own acceptance run is on a retention-sweep deletion clock and is unfrozen. Empirically settled or corrected today: the tool-results spill is real (three 32-40 KB files on disk) but the pointer is `<persisted-output>` text inside the tool_result content block, not `toolUseResult.persistedOutputPath` (0 such records exist) — T7 as written would silently never fire; `<runId>.json` lands under the session current at run END (journal under dd469822, snapshot under e423cd3c), so T8's path is permanently ENOENT; `workflowProgress` mixes `type:"workflow_phase"` rows whose every field is null with the real agent rows; `git stash create` fails on this zero-commit repo ("You do not have the initial commit yet", exit 1), making D7/T14's checkpoint inoperable; `[touch]` markers still have zero genuine instances while a naive grep returns 12 files of quoted marker prose, confirming SKILLS-6's precedence hazard; `inception.md`'s "~1.09M tokens" is exactly the banned `totalTokens` field (1,089,990 vs a true ~29.5M rollup); `.touch/` is still not gitignored in a repo with no commits; and the monitor on 8931 the docs point at now refuses connections while two decision_watchers keep running, one eleven hours past its run. Full findings, fixtures and recommendations in the findings file; the five decisions the synthesizer must make (not merely record) are listed at its end.

Scanned all operational state under .claude/local-orchestrators/ as data: parsed all three events.jsonl streams (821 lines, 100% valid JSON, zero malformed), all three .watcher-state.json checkpoints, all three orch-config.json files, the logs, and the folder layout — cross-checked against status.sh, decision_watcher.py, monitor_server.py, monitor.html, test_shell.py, .gitignore, and the D4/D5 decisions in touch-aggregator-plan.md. 18 findings: 1 blocker, 10 major, 5 minor, 2 nits.

Headline: the CLAUDE.md/inception.md/aggregator-workflow claim that these orch-configs point at an earlier "omnigent" project is FALSE. All three wf_dir values resolve under /home/agent/.claude/projects/-home-laniakea-Projects-touch/, all three directories exist, and each journal's byte size exactly equals the sibling checkpoint's offset (56741 / 15567 / 750) — this is this project's own live run history, and it is the only real corpus D4's legacy adapter can be built and tested against. The docs have been telling every agent to discount it (RUNSTATE-1).

Blocker for legacy ingest (RUNSTATE-2): legacy events carry no run id and no task id — the full observed key set is only ts/plan/stage/state/detail plus optional title/agent/tokens/quiet. Worse, touch-repo-recon/events.jsonl demonstrably spans two script invocations of one journal (a 13:41 wave of 5 agents replayed after the 13:50 seed lines, then a 13:50 wave of 4), and the run id appears only as free text inside one detail string. D4's ref.runId/ordinal must be synthesized (from orch-config wf_dir basename plus a per-(plan,stage) respawn counter) and that rule needs to be written down.

The streams are a better spec than the spec. Real, reproducible shapes an ingester must tolerate, none of them described in either plan: a fully successful run recorded as plan|failed "loop exited -> synthesis" while the checkpoint says plans.research=failed (RUNSTATE-4); checkpoints that contradict their own stream and are never closed on kill — touch-repo-recon lists 7 phantom running agents although its stream terminates with orchestrator|complete|done "stopped by user" (RUNSTATE-5); append order != timestamp order with two ISO formats mixed (status.sh emits +00:00, the watcher emits backdated journal Z stamps; 2/5/3 measured inversions) (RUNSTATE-6); every stage completion written twice by two writers with different details, 38 s apart, one with an agent field and one without (RUNSTATE-7); labels that collide six ways ("research #1" for all six parallel researchers), (plan,stage) that is not unique over time (two v0task agents), and orchestrator rows with no agent at all (RUNSTATE-8); and agents that never close because the DRIVER-1 stale-close guard is correctly gated on attempt strictly increasing while the respawn reused attempt=1 (RUNSTATE-9). Agent ids are also truncated to 8 chars in events but stored full 17-char in the checkpoint, so the two sources cannot be joined (RUNSTATE-3).

Two structural, do-this-first items: .gitignore has NO .touch/ entry even though D5 and P1 both require one, and D5 puts raw PTY capture and hook spools in that tree (RUNSTATE-10); and master has zero commits — git status shows only "?? .claude/", "?? .gitignore", "?? CLAUDE.md", "?? README.md", "?? inception.md" — so the 824 KB of run history CLAUDE.md:120 forbids deleting is one git clean -fdx from gone (RUNSTATE-11). Neither the aggregator plan nor the v0 plan (P1-P12) contains a legacy-ingest item at all.

Remaining minors: 91% of the legacy stream is per-delta token noise replayed in full on every connect (RUNSTATE-12); the folder layout is not uniform, so plan-only touch-monitor-spawn is listed as a task and orch-config.json cannot be assumed present (RUNSTATE-13); /tasks returns two different token shapes (RUNSTATE-14); the watcher stalls silently on in-place journal truncation, with all three offsets currently sitting exactly at EOF, and D6 mandates the missing rule for Touch's own tailer (RUNSTATE-15); status.sh validates nothing and CLAUDE.md's "no double quotes" rule is justified by a JSON claim I disproved empirically — the real reason is shell/JS-template embedding (RUNSTATE-16). Plus two nits on fixture realism and empty directories not surviving a clone.

All empirical probes ran in a throwaway dir under /tmp/claude-1000; nothing outside the mandated status.sh calls touched the live task folder.

result.summary: Reconciled all six research reports (~90 findings) into one plan that supersedes touch-aggregator-plan (T1-T23) and touch-monitor-spawn-plan (P1-P12), with an explicit D1-D14 disposition table. 20 global decisions settle every contested question: restart = re-invoke with stored partition + only:[ids] (resumeFromRunId rejected); role/model table with divider pinned Fable; three session classes (owned/cooperating/observed) with evidence-gated promotion; harness-first node identity; two run profiles (Workflow journal vs Agent-tool ledger); one marker grammar; plan-close semantics that stop recording green runs as failed; 5-member open-tail ref union; query-string API; 127.0.0.1+token+Origin security posture; full legacy-ingest rule set; .watcher-state.json gitignored and never read by Touch. 37 ordered items across 5 phases: phase 0 repo safety (gitignore before anything creates .touch/, git bootstrap to main, fixture freeze before the retention sweep, settling probes, docs truth pass, findings register), phase 1 monitoring-module fixes, phase 2 protocol/topology/restart/touch-orchestrate, phase 3 monitoring-only Touch v0 with zero control verbs, phase 4 control plane gated on the hook hot-reload probe. One inter-report contradiction was resolved empirically: git stash create on this zero-commit repo exits 1 with no sha (AUDIT-8 right, PLANS-9's exit-0 claim corrected). Merged-alias and discard registers included; the 161 prior-corpus findings get a register item (R-06) with a static test.
